title: Strange Footprints

beats.narrativeText: In the ground just outside the station, the expedition's field notes record something the learner wasn't expecting: a trail of footprints, and no explanation for whose they are.
Atlas offers a few possible explanations for the tracks. Several sound plausible on their own — but only one can actually fit every piece of evidence at once.
The learner measures the tracks carefully and lines up each measurement against the recorded evidence.
Comparing each possible explanation side by side reveals exactly where they agree with the evidence — and where they don't.
The learner's job isn't to guess the right answer — it's to rule out every explanation the evidence doesn't support, until only one is left standing.
Working through the evidence one explanation at a time, the learner arrives at a single conclusion — not a guess, but one they can actually defend.
The learner reflects on something that wasn't obvious at the start: ruling explanations out turned out to matter more than trying to guess the right one from the beginning.
Start to finish, this is the learner's first complete scientific investigation — and for the first time, their confidence as an Explorer feels earned rather than just given.

activities.title: Measure Tracks
activities.storyContext: A series of unusual footprints has been found outside the station, recorded in the expedition's field notes but never explained.
activities.instructions: Measure the length, width and spacing of the tracks, and record your measurements precisely — the exact numbers are what will let you rule things out later.
activities.output: A set of track measurements in the Explorer Journal.

activities.title: Compare Evidence
activities.storyContext: Atlas offers a few possible explanations for the tracks — each one sounds reasonable until you check it against the evidence.
activities.instructions: Compare your measurements with each possible explanation Atlas provides, one at a time.
activities.output: Notes comparing the evidence against each possible explanation.

activities.title: Identify Similarities and Differences
activities.storyContext: Only one explanation fits everything you've measured — the rest will fall apart under close comparison.
activities.instructions: For each possible explanation, identify exactly where it matches your evidence and where it doesn't.
activities.output: A list of similarities and differences for each explanation.

activities.title: Justify Conclusions
activities.storyContext: Explorer Academy doesn't want your best guess — it wants a conclusion you can defend by explaining why every other option fails.
activities.instructions: Explain which explanation the evidence best supports, and for each of the others, name the specific evidence that rules it out.
activities.output: A justified conclusion supported by evidence.

activities.title: Create a Field Guide of Track Patterns
activities.storyContext: A field guide would help future Explorers identify tracks more quickly.
activities.instructions: Sketch a simple field guide describing a few different track patterns.
activities.output: An illustrated field guide of track patterns.

activities.title: How Do Wildlife Researchers Identify Animals?
activities.storyContext: Identifying an animal from tracks alone is a real scientific skill.
activities.instructions: Find out how wildlife researchers identify animals without ever seeing them.
activities.output: None required — this is an open investigation.

prompts: Which explanation did you rule out first, and what specific piece of evidence made you eliminate it?

discussionPoints: Which explanations did you rule out, and why?
How did measuring help you decide between explanations?
parentGuide.preparation: A ruler or tape measure is useful for measuring tracks.
parentGuide.assessment: Look for a conclusion that is justified by eliminating alternatives, not just a guess.

completionCriteria: Tracks measured, evidence compared, and a single well-supported conclusion justified.
